summary: Pages 47-113 and 134-137 of the host PDF are stray pages of South Korean Interim Government Activities No. 22 (July 1947), misbound into the May 1948 issue; pages 114-133 are absent. The text is the tail of Section 1 (paragraphs 22-57) and fragments of Section 2 (Legal and Public Safety). Contents: Marshall's speech and Acting Military Governor Helmick's statements on American aid and food-export rumors; Korea Civil Service; the Interim Legislative Assembly's passage of the Anti-Collaborator Bill as the Special Law on National Traitors, Collaborators and Profiteers and its second reading of a Temporary Constitution; the dispute over transferring governors; Rightist and Leftist trends and the assassination of Lyuh Woon Hyung; verbatim American and Soviet statements on the Joint Commission deadlock over consultation with anti-trusteeship parties; mail exchanges, repatriation, courts, police installations and prison population. The identification as No. 22 / July 1947 is confirmed by the text: all dated events fall in July 1947 and the statistics refer to June 1947.
highlights: Anti-Collaborator Bill completed second reading 2 July as the Special Law Dealing with National Traitors, Collaborators, and Profiteers; third reading omitted.
Temporary Constitution of Korea (Chosun): second reading of all seven chapters concluded 29-31 July, local-government Part D begun 31 July.
Assembly voted 39-22 on 9 July to return the transfer of four officials, ruling it had no jurisdiction under Ordinance 118.
Lyuh Woon Hyung, Laboring People's Party leader, shot dead in Seoul on 19 July; suspect Hahn Chi Kun.
Joint Commission deadlocked over admitting Anti-Trusteeship Committee parties; Soviet side noted 70 million claimed members across applicants.
US count of parties: 71 rightist (19.3 million claimed members) against 75 leftist (32.3 million) under the Soviet list.
Civilian Supply Program aid May 1946-March 1947 stated as 91 million dollars, with 395,836 metric tons of grain.
June 1947 prison population in South Korea totalled 19,833, of whom 17,216 were sentenced.

sections.title: Section 1 (continued): Government and Politics, paragraphs 22-57
sections.summary: Continuation of the July 1947 general section (opening pages and section title not in the excerpt): aid statements, civil service, Assembly business, politics, Joint Commission, interzone mail and foreign affairs.

sections.title: American aid to Korea and food-export rumors
sections.summary: Secretary Marshall's 1 July speech rejecting charges of American imperialism was translated and released in Korean on 8 July. On 9 July the Acting Military Governor reported 91 million dollars of civilian supply aid, May 1946 to March 1947, including 395,836 tons of grain. On 19 July he denounced rumors of food export as malicious lies.

sections.title: Korea Civil Service
sections.summary: The Training Division of the Office of Korea Civil Service completed procedures for Performance Rating Reports, required for the first time of provincial and national employees. They are due in the first fifteen days of August from staff with at least six months' service. Clerical examinations continued in provincial cities and larger towns.

sections.title: Korean Interim Legislative Assembly: Anti-Collaborator Bill
sections.summary: After resuming on 30 June, the Assembly passed the remaining collaborator paragraphs (votes such as 32-14 and 42-6) and the profiteer chapter, mostly by common consent. On 2 July it retitled the measure the Special Law Dealing with National Traitors, Collaborators, and Profiteers, adopted a three-year limit, and omitted a third reading. On 7 July it assigned drafting of special-court rules to the original drafters.

sections.title: The Temporary Constitution of Democratic Korea (Chosun)
sections.summary: A compromise revised draft of the Temporary Constitution was presented on 7 July and, despite Leftist protests, passed to second reading on 11 July. The word "democratic" was dropped from the title, 31 to 8. Chapters on rights and duties (including labor management participation), the Assembly, executive, bureaus, courts, finance and supplementary rules were then adopted, mostly by common consent. Local government (Section 36) began 31 July.

sections.title: Assignment of officials
sections.summary: On 8 July the Assembly debated the Civil Administrator's proposed transfer of governors Park Keun Hon, Sunn Min Ho and Park Chong Man, and Civil Service director Chung Il Hyung. The debate turned on whether Ordinance 118 required confirmation. On 9 July the Assembly voted 39 to 22 to return the communication, for lack of jurisdiction.

sections.title: Clarification of Assembly authority (Ordinance 118)
sections.summary: On 28 July Civil Administrator Ahn and Justice Director Kim Pyong No appeared at the Assembly's request. Kim held that Ordinance 118 leaves Military Government supreme and able to legislate without Assembly approval. Suh U Sok and Yang Che Pak disputed this and invoked the Assembly's power to review appointments. Kim urged the Assembly to adopt a constitution.

sections.title: The Franchise Law
sections.summary: On 31 July the Assembly took up the Acting Military Governor's 21 July letter asking it to reconsider franchise provisions: the age limit of twenty-three, exclusion of ex-prisoners, traitors and senior Japanese-era officials, and votes for recent arrivals from North Korea. Members defended the age limit; no formal action followed, and the matter went to the Legislative and Judicial Committee, 44 to 0.

sections.title: Attendance of representatives, July 1947
sections.summary: Table of the Assembly's July 1947 sessions 102 to 120, showing the date, the number of registered members present (from 55 on 15 July to 76 on 9 July, of 90 authorized) and the presiding official, either Vice-Speaker Choe Tong O or Yun Ki Sop. Quorum is 45 to hold session and 60 to consider measures.

sections.title: Political Activities: the Right
sections.summary: Rightist expectations of the Joint Commission declined in July because of the Soviet delegation's attitude. On 4 July, 150 representatives of about seventy Rightist organizations rejected General Brown's criticism and General Hodge's letter to Rhee, demanded a general election, called for Ahn's resignation, and demanded suspension of the Labor Party's newspaper.

sections.title: Political Activities: the Left
sections.summary: The Left continued to brand Rightists as pro-Japanese traitors and sought their exclusion from consultation. Five parties issued a joint statement on 10 July and four more on 19 July, the latter demanding consultation only with parties supporting the Moscow Decision. Lyuh Woon Hyung was shot dead on 19 July by Hahn Chi Kun, and the Nation Saving Society was ordered dissolved.

sections.title: Political Activities: General (Presidential envoy)
sections.summary: The State Department's announcement that Lt. Gen. Albert C. Wedemeyer would go to Korea as President Truman's special envoy brightened the Rightist outlook. Rightist leaders welcomed the news and shifted their attention from the Joint Commission to the expected survey. The Leftist press barely mentioned it, and Leftist leaders offered no comment.

sections.title: US-USSR Joint Commission
sections.summary: The Joint Commission met in Pyongyang on 2-3 July, then deadlocked in Seoul over which parties to consult. Brown (15 July) and Soviet chief Shtikov (21 July) set out positions on local groups and Anti-Trusteeship Committee members. Koreans in Japan sent support. Brown spoke on 27 and 31 July, with party tables showing 71 Rightist and 75 Leftist parties.

sections.title: Interzone Activities
sections.summary: Mail was exchanged with North Korea twice in July. On 12 July, 10,643 letters, 1,703 cards and 537 registered items went north, and 3,502 letters, 634 cards and 387 registered items came south. On 26 July, 10,108 letters, 1,568 cards and 542 registered items went north; 4,908, 1,378 and 369 came south.

sections.title: Foreign Affairs
sections.summary: As of 26 July, 18,672 Koreans caught entering Japan illegally had been apprehended in Japan and 416 in Korean waters; 300 permits went to Chinese for repatriation. Dr. Moon Chang Wook left on 22 July to seek sponsors for at least fifty students in American colleges. A table lists July repatriation ships at Pusan.

sections.title: Section 2 (fragment): Legal and Public Safety
sections.summary: Opening of Section 2 plus detached later pages (police installations and prisons); pages 114-133 are absent from the excerpt.

sections.title: Legal
sections.summary: Chief Justice Kim Young Moo's directive brought criminal dockets current by 20 July, though civil cases remain backlogged. Juvenile courts tried 154 cases in 1945, 1,700 in 1946 and 1,240 in the first five months of 1947. Twenty-nine law probationers became judges and prosecutors, and 2,500 law books were loaned to the National Law Library.

sections.title: Public Safety: police installations and prisons
sections.summary: A table gives 1,977 South Korean police installations as of 1 Feb. 1947: 156 stations, 414 boxes, 1,495 sub-stations and 68 branches. Kwangju Prison had about 500 prisoners working its farm and workshops; 10,000 blankets reached the Justice Department by 19 July. June 1947 prisons held 19,833 (17,216 sentenced; 181 women).
